CHIEF COMPLAINT
Acne on the face.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient presents with acne on the face that began approximately two years ago and occurs most every day. She has been using over-the-counter treatments including Persa-Gel and regular facial washing with elf facial cleanser (super clarity cleanser), which provides some benefit. She denies associated symptoms including itching, bleeding, or pain. Current skincare routine consists of: morning - wiping face with water and washcloth, occasionally using elf cleanser if skin feels greasy; evening - elf facial cleanser, toner, and Persa-Gel. Acne is mild to moderate on the face with minimal involvement of the chest and back. She describes today as a "good day" for acne. She denies acne flaring with menses and reports regular menstrual periods for approximately two years. Mother notes the most significant flare occurred when patient started school sports in the fall, attributed to increased sweating. Despite good adherence to skincare regimen, improvement has been limited.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies itching, bleeding, or pain associated with acne. Reports regular menstrual periods. Remainder of review of systems not documented.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
None documented.

MEDICATIONS
- Persa-Gel (over-the-counter)
- Elf facial cleanser (super clarity cleanser, over-the-counter)
- Facial toner (over-the-counter)
- Sunscreen SPF 30

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
No additional family history noted.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Lives with parents and sister. Pets include a dog, bird, and bunnies. Currently in 7th grade. Participates in basketball, volleyball, and tap dance. Uses sunscreen SPF 30 during summer.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Full general examination performed except for areas under underwear and bra. Skin examination reveals multiple benign nevi on trunk and extremities, scattered skin-colored papules, open and closed comedones, and erythematous papules on face with primary distribution on forehead and some involvement of central cheeks and chin. Chest and back relatively spared. Multiple benign moles noted on arms, legs, back, and abdomen with normal appearance and no worrisome features. Remainder of physical examination normal.

RESULTS
No laboratory studies performed.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Mild to moderate acne, predominantly comedonal with small inflammatory component.

Plan:
1. Initiate topical therapy: Morning routine - wash face with mild cleanser, then apply noncomedogenic moisturizer with SPF 30 or higher. Evening routine - wash face with mild cleanser, allow to dry, apply adapalene 0.1% cream in thin layer to affected areas. Patient instructed to start adapalene use a few nights per week, gradually increasing to nightly use. If adapalene is expensive or not covered by insurance, may substitute with over-the-counter alternative gel. Follow with Persa-Gel in thin layer to affected areas, then apply noncomedogenic moisturizer.
2. Counseled that topical retinoid use may cause skin sensitivity, dryness, and irritation. Patient advised to wear sunscreen SPF 30 or higher when outdoors.
3. Follow-up appointment in six months to assess response to treatment and acne progression.
4. Multiple benign moles identified on examination. Will monitor; no intervention required at this time.
